pharm: Promotes wakefulness through an incompletely understood mechanism with sympathomimetic-like properties, including binding to the dopamine transporter and inhibition of dopamine reuptake.
quick: Narcolepsy/OSA: 200 mg once daily in the AM; SWD: 200 mg ~1 hr before shift
Take once daily; food does not affect overall bioavailability (may delay peak ~1 hr)
May cause fetal harm (animal data); use only if benefit justifies risk
Excretion in milk unknown; use caution in nursing women
No specific adjustment; severe renal failure did not alter modafinil kinetics
Severe hepatic impairment: reduce to one-half the usual dose
Skin/rash, psychiatric symptoms, blood pressure/heart rate, signs of dependence
summary: Modafinil is a Schedule IV wakefulness-promoting agent indicated to improve wakefulness in adults with excessive sleepiness due to narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), or shift work disorder (SWD). It is habit forming and shares some properties with CNS stimulants. In OSA it treats sleepiness but is not a substitute for CPAP. It carries warnings for serious, potentially life-threatening skin reactions (SJS, TEN, DRESS), angioedema/anaphylaxis, multi-organ hypersensitivity, and psychiatric symptoms.
indications: Excessive sleepiness associated with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) (adults; adjunct to CPAP, not a substitute)
Excessive sleepiness associated with shift work disorder (SWD) (adults)

dosage.n: Doses up to 400 mg/day tolerated but no consistent added benefit over 200 mg

dosage.t: Approximately 1 hour before the start of the work shift

dosage.d: Reduce to one-half the recommended dose

dosage.n: Elimination may be reduced with aging; monitor closely

admin: Give once daily; for narcolepsy/OSA take in the morning
For shift work disorder take about 1 hour before the shift
May be taken with or without food (food may delay the time to peak by about 1 hour)
Halve the dose in severe hepatic impairment
moa: The mechanism by which modafinil promotes wakefulness is not fully known. It has wake-promoting actions similar to sympathomimetic agents such as amphetamine and methylphenidate, though its pharmacologic profile is not identical. Modafinil binds to the dopamine transporter and inhibits dopamine reuptake in vitro, an action associated in vivo with increased extracellular dopamine; wake-promoting activity is dopamine-transporter dependent in animal models. Its wakefulness effect is attenuated by the alpha-1 antagonist prazosin.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to modafinil or armodafinil or its inactive ingredients
relative: History of psychosis, depression, or mania
Known cardiovascular disease, recent MI, or unstable angina
History of left ventricular hypertrophy or mitral valve prolapse syndrome on prior CNS stimulants
History of drug or stimulant abuse (habit forming, Schedule IV)
monitor: Skin for rash or signs of severe cutaneous reaction
Psychiatric symptoms (anxiety, mania, psychosis, suicidal ideation)

preg: Based on animal data, modafinil may cause fetal harm. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women; intrauterine growth restriction and spontaneous abortion have been reported with modafinil and armodafinil. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. Steroidal contraceptives may be less effective with modafinil, increasing the risk of unintended pregnancy.
lact: It is not known whether modafinil or its metabolites are excreted in human milk. Because many drugs are excreted in human milk, caution should be exercised when modafinil is administered to a nursing woman.
renal: Severe chronic renal failure (creatinine clearance <=20 mL/min) did not significantly affect the pharmacokinetics of modafinil after a single 200 mg dose, although exposure to the inactive metabolite modafinil acid increased 9-fold. No specific dosage adjustment is provided.
hepatic: In severe hepatic impairment, reduce the dose to one-half the usual amount. In cirrhosis the oral clearance of modafinil was decreased by about 60% and steady-state concentration was doubled compared with normal patients.

major: Steroidal contraceptives (e.g., ethinyl estradiol): reduced effectiveness; use alternative/additional contraception during and for 1 month after modafinil
CYP2C19 substrates (phenytoin, diazepam, propranolol, omeprazole, clomipramine, TCAs): exposure may increase; consider dose adjustment
Warfarin: monitor prothrombin time/INR more frequently
moderate: Cyclosporine: blood levels may be reduced; monitor concentrations
Strong CYP3A4/5 inducers (carbamazepine, phenobarbital, rifampin) or inhibitors (ketoconazole, erythromycin): may alter modafinil levels
CYP3A4/5 substrates (midazolam, triazolam): exposure may be reduced
interactions.food: Food does not affect overall bioavailability but may delay the time to peak concentration by about 1 hour.
interactions.alcohol: Use with alcohol has not been studied; it is prudent to avoid alcohol.
interactions.diagnostics: Mean GGT and alkaline phosphatase may rise; few patients have values outside the normal range.

serious: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)
Psychiatric symptoms (mania, delusions, hallucinations, suicidal ideation, aggression)
Cardiovascular events (chest pain, palpitations, transient ischemic ECG changes)
emergency: Angioedema or anaphylaxis (facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing)
Acute psychiatric crisis or suicidal ideation

monitoring: Skin for early signs of rash; discontinue at first sign unless clearly not drug-related
Psychiatric status (anxiety, depression, mania, psychosis, suicidality)
Heart rate and blood pressure, especially in cardiovascular disease
Degree of sleepiness and continued need for CPAP in OSA
counsel: Stop the drug and call your doctor right away for any rash, hives, mouth sores, blisters, peeling skin, or trouble swallowing/breathing
This medicine is not a replacement for sleep; do not assume your wakefulness is normal before driving or operating machinery
If you have OSA, keep using your CPAP
Use an additional or alternative method of contraception if on hormonal birth control, during and for 1 month after treatment
Avoid alcohol; report chest pain, depression, anxiety, or signs of psychosis or mania
This medication is habit forming (Schedule IV); take only as prescribed
pk: Peak plasma concentration at 2 to 4 hours
Effective elimination half-life about 15 hours after multiple doses
Long; supports once-daily dosing (steady state in 2-4 days)
pearls: Schedule IV and habit forming; shares reinforcing/stimulant-like properties
Serious rash (SJS/TEN/DRESS) typically appears within 1-5 weeks of starting; discontinue at first sign of rash
Reduces effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives via CYP3A4 induction
In OSA, treats sleepiness only; maximize CPAP before and during therapy
Halve the dose in severe hepatic impairment
missed: If you miss your morning dose, take it as soon as you remember earlier in the day; do not take it late in the day as it can cause insomnia. Skip the dose if it is close to bedtime and resume your normal schedule. Do not double up.
overdose: Symptoms include insomnia, restlessness, disorientation, confusion, agitation, anxiety, excitation, hallucination, nausea, diarrhea, and cardiovascular changes such as tachycardia, bradycardia, hypertension, and chest pain. Fatal overdoses have been reported, alone or with other drugs. There is no specific antidote; manage with supportive care including cardiovascular monitoring.
